purpose: Defines which source types MathBridge should use for each layer of a curriculum comparison and prevents a single source from being stretched beyond its authority.

comparison_layers.rule: Curriculum requirements must come from official curriculum/standards or an approved textbook sequence; classroom resources cannot establish statutory expectations.
Teaching-method claims should be tied to explicit guidance, textbook evidence or observed lesson design. Avoid national stereotypes.
Explanations of pedagogical rationale should distinguish official intent from research evidence and from MathBridge interpretation.
Examples must be labelled as examples, not as universal descriptions of every classroom in that system.
Research claims should eventually link to specific papers, reviews or evidence-rated practice guides rather than only umbrella organisations.

publication_rules: Every visible curriculum claim must have at least one source_id.
Claims presented as official requirements require an authority-level 5 source.
Claims comparing national teaching cultures should normally have multiple evidence types and be phrased cautiously.
Exact quotations require a source locator and page/section/standard code where available.
Teacher-facing summaries should normally paraphrase rather than reproduce long source text.
US mode must identify whether a statement refers to Common Core, a specific state, or a classroom-resource example.
China mode must distinguish national curriculum stage requirements from PEP textbook year-by-year sequencing.
Legacy and current textbook editions must never be silently mixed.
